RALLY / EVOLUTION LAB12 policy inputs → 2 driving outputs / Neuroevolution
UNDER THE HOOD

Learning, one lap at a time.

48 neural drivers share a procedurally generated gravel circuit. Each driver sees 12 inputs: upcoming road direction, sideways offset, speed, sliding, curvature, slope, tire load, previous steering and a bias.

Two neural outputs control steering and throttle / brake. After each generation, the best drivers survive; their weights are combined and mutated to create the next population. After 25 generations without improvement, mutation increases and fresh drivers enter while the champion survives.

Finish first. Then go faster. Completing a lap always beats an incomplete attempt. Once drivers finish, shorter lap times earn higher scores.

This lightweight simulation includes tire grip, sliding, drag, road gradient and elevation-dependent tire load. It uses a noisy road-following starting policy, not a pretrained driver. It is an educational model, not a full vehicle dynamics simulator.

New tracks retain the best policy to test transfer. Export or copy a driver link to save its exact weights and track settings. Links evaluate the driver locally before showing a lap time. The racing line shows up to four improved champion laps, colored by speed. Choose 3, 6 or 10 km circuits; each has four timed sectors. Attempt limits scale with course length. The minimap tracks the current leader, and the Follow car camera keeps the driving visible on long courses. Algorithm comparison gives each method the same evaluation budget; results describe this one track and random seed, not a universal winner. Training runs entirely in this tab; closing it ends the session.
